description:
FILED s449 (Fable, round-7 review of agent Q) from an own-probe misfire whose divergence survived the clean re-probe.  PRE-EXISTING on main c8a8311 -- nothing to do with the dup work; reproduces on a plain empty file.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
    local $/;
    open(my $fh, "<", $empty_file) or die;
    my $x = <$fh>;          # perl: defined, length 0     PCL: undef
    my $y = <$fh>;          # perl: undef                 PCL: undef
Line mode ($/ = "\n") answers undef on both sides -- the quirk is slurp-only.
Same shape through an fdopen of an exhausted descriptor: open(my $d, "<&=" . fileno($s)) after $s slurped -- perl def[0], PCL undef.

Perl rule: in slurp mode the FIRST readline returns everything from here to EOF, and "nothing" is the empty string, a defined value; only a repeat read answers undef.  Programs test defined() on a slurp to mean "the open handle was readable at all".

FIX SHAPE: %p-readline-impl (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) slurp arm answers "" instead of nil the first time; needs a per-read decision, not per-handle state -- perl re-answers "" after a seek back to EOF (probe that before implementing).  BAR: the three-row repro above + the seek-back probe + a nonempty-file inverse vs perl; a Pl/t guard row; cl/ change so the io/ companion leg at the next sweep.
subject: Slurp mode reads a DEFINED empty string on the FIRST read at EOF -- perl <$fh> with $/ undef on an empty (or exhausted) stream is "" once, then undef; PCL answers undef immediately
